body_text:
A nonzero element $a$ of a commutative ring is a zero divisor
if $ab=0$ for some nonzero $b$. An integral domain is a
nontrivial commutative ring without zero divisors. Every field
is an integral domain, but the converse fails; the integers
form the standard example.
